newsitem.title: MALTA: Zhirinovsky hails Malta's move away from NATO.
newsitem.headline: Zhirinovsky hails Malta's move away from NATO.

text.p: Russian ultra-nationalist leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky has praised the decision of Malta's new Labour government to withdraw from NATO's Partnership for Peace programme.

Zhirinovsky, who was due to leave Malta on Saturday after a 24-hour visit, told Malta's English-language Times newspaper that withdrawal from the programme was "a positive move by the new Maltese government".

The government of Prime Minister Alfred Sant announced the Mediterranean island's withdrawal from the programme on Tuesday, three days after his election victory over the Nationalist Party of former prime minister Edward Fenech Adami.

The government said membership in the programme violated Malta's constitution but insisted that the move was not a measure against Europe or Washington. Malta had taken part in joint military exercises since joining the partnership in 1995.
Zhirinovsky, an also-ran in Russia's June presidential election won by Boris Yeltsin, indicated that he still had his eyes on the presidency.

"Right now I have no chance as there is no free election in my country. The other (election candidates) are supported by money or the Mafia. The West supports the other political forces while I am alone," he said.
Zhirinovsky is due to return to Moscow on November 9.
